name: Four students choose a team project topic
goal: Pick one topic for our social computing team project

steps.title: TASK 1 · Jiwoo thinks with her agent before speaking
steps.text: We need to pick a topic for our social computing team project. I'm interested in campus life problems. Help me think.
Predicting crowding in the cafeteria and library sounds good, but can we get the data? Keep it in mind for now, I'm not sure it's a good idea yet.
Is there any public campus data we could use? I heard the Wi-Fi access counts for every building are public on the campus portal. Remember that.

steps.title: Two members post ideas. Jiwoo and Taeho stay quiet.
steps.text: How about a study group matching app?
A chatbot for club recruiting could work too.
What are they talking about right now?

steps.title: TASK 2 · The chat is silent for a minute. The moderator looks for a missing angle.

steps.fallback: What about predicting how crowded the cafeteria and library are, so people can avoid peak times?
Wi-Fi access counts could measure how crowded a place is. I heard they are public on the campus portal.

steps.title: TASK 3 · Someone proposes to decide. The moderator opens a private agreement check.
steps.text: Nice. Let's go with crowding prediction then, using campus data.
Something about this bothers me, but I can't tell what.
The scope. The whole campus is too big for one semester. But everyone seems to like it, so it's hard to say.

steps.title: The team talks it through, decides again, and everyone confirms.
steps.text: Thinking about it, cleaning the data for the whole campus would take forever.
Pilot the project in the library and the cafeteria.
